tool_args.old_string: Multi-turn dialogue performance in LLMs degrades as conversations grow longer. Dongre et al. (2026) quantified this through the Goal Attention Ratio (GAR), showing 27-48% drops over 50 turns, while their residual stream probes reveal that goal information persists (AUC up to 0.98) even as the attention channel closes. This creates a natural hypothesis: if the information is in the residual stream but attention fails to access it, a learnable gate on the residual connection should recover it. We implement this hypothesis as ThreadGate, a per-layer gating module trained with joint NTP and GAR objectives. ThreadGate successfully optimizes GAR during training (0.02 to 0.48), but this improvement completely fails to transfer to inference (GAR = 0.016, a 30x gap). Through systematic analysis, we identify three coupled failure mechanisms: (1) NTP loss dominates gate gradients, causing gates to learn reverse turn conditioning (suppressing in early turns where GAR is high, becoming passive in late turns where GAR is low); (2) the resulting attention pattern overfits to training data and does not generalize; (3) at inference time, gates attenuate residual updates by only 2-7%, far too weak to shift attention patterns. Four-way ablation (ThreadGate vs. Uniform Gate vs. LoRA-only vs. Base) confirms gating provides zero incremental contribution. Combined with Dongre et al.'s independent failure of goal re-injection, our results suggest that simple attention steering approaches face fundamental obstacles from NTP optimization pressure.
tool_args.new_string: Multi-turn dialogue performance in LLMs degrades as conversations grow longer. Dongre et al. (2026) quantified this through the Goal Attention Ratio (GAR), showing 27-48% drops over 50 turns, while their residual stream probes reveal that goal information persists (AUC up to 0.98) even as the attention channel closes. This creates a natural hypothesis: if the information is in the residual stream but attention fails to access it, a learnable gate on the residual connection should recover it. We implement this hypothesis as ThreadGate, a per-layer gating module trained with joint NTP and GAR objectives. ThreadGate successfully optimizes GAR during training (0.02 to 0.48), but this improvement completely fails to transfer to inference (GAR = 0.016, a 30x gap). Our central finding is that teacher-forcing training creates a fundamental distribution shift: attention patterns learned under teacher-forced contexts do not generalize to autoregressive generation, where the model conditions on its own outputs. This distribution shift is structural, independent of loss design or gating architecture. We further identify two coupled mechanisms that amplify the shift: (1) NTP loss dominates gate gradients, causing gates to learn reverse turn conditioning (suppressing at early turns where GAR is high, becoming passive at late turns where intervention is needed); (2) at inference time, gates attenuate residual updates by only 2-7%, far too weak to shift attention patterns. Four-way ablation (ThreadGate vs. Uniform Gate vs. LoRA-only vs. Base) confirms gating provides zero incremental contribution. Combined with Dongre et al.'s independent failure of goal re-injection, our results demonstrate that auxiliary attention losses optimized under teacher-forcing face a fundamental generalization barrier.

**SP2: 量化三个具体失败机制。** 不是 "X doesn't work" 的简单报告，而是: (1) NTP-GAR 梯度冲突的逐层量化; (2) 30x 泛化 gap 的训练轨迹追踪; (3) gate 干预强度的定量评估。为后续工作提供具体的 failure mode taxonomy。

**SP4: 与 Dongre 形成 convergent evidence。** 两种独立干预路线 (Dongre 的 goal re-injection + 我们的 residual gating) 均失败，共同指向 NTP 优化压力下 attention steering 的根本困难。

**SP5: 三阶段训练动力学。** v7 展现 plateau → phase transition → convergence 的清晰训练动力学，证明 MSE 双向 loss 设计本身是 sound 的，问题在泛化而非训练。
